chunk_map.heading: # Map the gaps, read your stack (title + lede)
## Phase 1: Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps
## Read the contrast, push back where it generalises
## Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed
## Say go, unless the cut spreads past the one rule
## Phase 2: Find the work you repeat across your stack
## Scan your history for the work that recurs
## Draw your top work-shapes as diagrams
## Sidestep: check your menu against the field's
## Decide what crosses back to your main repo

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Traced every pronoun/demonstrative/named-thing across all 10 chunks in sequential order. 'M4'/'M5'/'M5 worktree' (chunk 0-1) are cross-module backward references, checked in the module file (see rule 3). 'it' in chunk 1's 'Point it at the coordinates' resolves to 'the agent' in the same sentence. 'the verifier' (chunk 2, line 33) resolves to the prompt block's 'a verifier wired to run on a cadence' (chunk 1, line 27's expanded prompt, same file, immediately prior chunk). 'In place' (chunk 4, line 47) resolves to chunk 3's prompt 'Cut it from ./CLAUDE.local.md in place' (immediately prior chunk). 'the next two prompts' (chunk 6, line 58) is a forward pointer, but it names a count and a reading-order sequence rather than requiring the reader to already know their content -- resolved as a reading-order pointer under §12's fallback, not a §1 violation. 'the handoff prompt' (chunk 8, line 89, 'What happened') is never defined inside this exercise file itself, but the enclosing module file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md line 19 names it in its '## What You'll Learn' bullet ('Generalize the shapes you mapped into a handoff prompt that builds your workflow skills across your stack') -- verified this bullet sits before the exercise's include-link at line 37 in the module file, so the module-include-order carve-out applies verbatim (the compendium's own worked example is 'the test-strategy skill' named in What You'll Learn). 'the kit you grow later' (chunk 8, line 81) is not established in this file or in the module's pre-include sections (What You'll Learn / Prework), but 'the kit' is used as established cross-arc vocabulary in multiple earlier-arc lectures (what-packaging-is.md, the-loop-has-a-name.md, module-2-prework.md) -- treated as arc-earned spine vocabulary under §1's carve-out; even if premature, that is a check_writing.md §14 concern per §1's own text, not a slides-class flag. No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found that isn't covered by a stated carve-out.

grep -n '\[.*\](' curriculum/exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md -> no output (confirmed by signals.has_urls: false). Body carries zero markdown links, so no cross-file positional-callback shape exists to evaluate. The session-artifact references to 'the M5 worktree' / task.md / plan.md name the source directly (not by page position) and fall under the module-arc/session-artifact carve-outs in §1.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -rn 'm5.*worktree\|Module 6' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/*.md confirms M4 (run-the-first-experiment.md) and M5 (learn-from-the-test.md) are real prior modules with the exact artefacts this file backward-references: learn-from-the-test.md:208 names 'M5 worktree branch... m5/<task-slug> branch in worktree at ../<repo>-m5, forked from M4's m4/<task-slug> SHA' and :213-214 name './CLAUDE.local.md' and './observations/' carried into the M5 worktree -- matching this file's 'the m4/<slug> branch recorded in task.md' / 'the m5/<slug> branch recorded in plan.md' / './CLAUDE.local.md' beats exactly. cross_module instance confirms the M4-M5-M6 set is registered together (curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/learn-from-the-test.md:158: 'cross_module @37aa983b: PASS -- set=[run-the-first-experiment,learn-from-the-test,spot-gaps-build-the-loop]'). No dangling beat reference.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in the body -- this exercise is a diff-and-diagnose task plus a history scan, not a live-demo beat with a narrated outcome the student is asked to guess ahead of.

Closest candidates by word/bullet count (via check-slide-size.js --report) are chunk 9 'Decide what crosses back to your main repo' (50 words, 0 bullets) and chunk 4 'Say go, unless the cut spreads past the one rule' (55 words, 2 bullets) -- both carry a complete, self-standing instruction (what crosses back and how; when to say go and where to cap the diff), not a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet. Every chunk in the 9-chunk deck carries either a multi-bullet setup, a prompt block, or a substantive standalone paragraph.

Checked all 9 body '##' headers against their own chunk content: 'Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed' -> chunk body cuts a stale rule via the prompt; 'Say go, unless the cut spreads past the one rule' -> chunk body is exactly that guardrail; 'Sidestep: check your menu against the field's' -> chunk compares the student's checking primitives against a field-sourced list; 'Decide what crosses back to your main repo' -> chunk states exactly what crosses back and how. No header is contradicted by its own chunk's content.

Checked all sub-items across all 10 chunks: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction found; no anaphora/epistrophe triple found; no self-grading superlative ('one of the most useful moves...') found -- closest is chunk 0's 'two runs are enough to place every lesson', a claim about the method's sufficiency, not self-grading praise of this exercise; no number-with-its-own-retraction pattern found (body carries no bare percentages/counts of this shape); no abstraction-noun stack found; no empty-leg verb triplet found. All sub-items PASS, including the blocking self-grading-superlative sub-item.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Scanned body for maintainer-dialect terms (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections-as-proper-noun). None appear. 'Diagnosis surfaced rules that turned out wrong' (chunk 3) uses 'surfaced' as the ordinary engineering verb ('revealed'), the explicitly exempted usage, not surface-as-noun. 'Packaging' and 'verifier' are AE101-taught student vocabulary from the M5 lecture (curriculum/lectures/what-packaging-is.md), not repo-internal authoring jargon.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -n '\*\*[^*]*\*\*' over raw body lines 1-94: every bold span is a short widget/label handle (<=5 words: 'Time:', 'Session', 'What you do:', 'What you build:', 'The point:', 'What happened:', 'Note') plus two bolded blockquote-callout leads ('Fast operator?' and 'Cut the scan when the top patterns are clear enough to use.' at chunk 6; 'Want to see the shapes, not read them?' at chunk 7). The second of these is an 11-word bolded full sentence, over the <=5-word handle cap on its face, but the maintainer block's dated Emphasis-pass note (raw line 101, 2026-07-09, citing check_slides.md §9 by name) explicitly states 'widget/label chrome and blockquote callouts untouched' as a deliberate decision, and the dispatch preamble requires checking for an existing accept-note before flagging a passage -- treated as maintainer-attested, accept-with-note, no edit owed. No bullet in the body opens with a bolded lead (the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture this rule bans); the 2026-07-09 pass explicitly de-bolded those.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content -- verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File is included via the ordinary exercise link ([Spot gaps, build the loop](exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md)) under the module file's '## Start here' section (curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md:37), which composes into a standard '.phase--exercise' wrapper -- the same inclusion path nearly every AE101 exercise uses. The file carries no internal '<!--flag:...-->' conditional wrapping of its own body (checked via full read), so it renders unconditionally whenever M6 is in the module set, and no prework/supplementary-shaped subsection (the 2026-07-09 failure mode) is present to be dropped.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js curriculum/exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md --report` -> zero rows for this file in the corpus-wide report (the 5 'ok' rows returned all belong to other files). grep -inE '(above|below|further down|at the top of this|see below)' over the raw body also returned zero hits; the two 'at the top of' occurrences (chunk 1 and its prompt) point at a position inside a different file the student holds ('the protected Run coordinates block at the top of plan.md'), a real physical location in an external artefact, not a same-page geometry pointer that dies at this file's own slide cut. Chunk 6's 'the next two prompts' is a reading-order forward pointer (allowed fallback), not a page-position one.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All 9 body '##' headers checked: 'Phase 1: Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps' / 'Phase 2: Find the work you repeat across your stack' are phase labels; 'Read the contrast, push back where it generalises', 'Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed', 'Say go, unless the cut spreads past the one rule', 'Scan your history for the work that recurs', 'Draw your top work-shapes as diagrams', 'Sidestep: check your menu against the field's', 'Decide what crosses back to your main repo' are all imperatives. Zero declarative-claim headers -- consistent with this file not being one of the two corpus declaratives the compendium's 2026-08-15 measurement names (close-the-ticket.md, fix-tests-first.md); this exercise has no beat where the file stops instructing to name a standalone law, so a label heading is correct throughout, not a missed declarative moment.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every bullet in all 10 chunks against the three classes. Closest candidate is chunk 3's 'Rules-files have a half-life. Adding rules is only half of it; subtracting the dead ones is the other half.' (line 38) -- this reads like doctrine, but it is the FIRST and only statement of this framing anywhere in this file (nothing earlier in the body already made this claim), so it is origination, not restatement of a split/lens already landed; stays in. The diff against pin 1abb84c6 shows the maintainer's own 2026-08-25 Lean pass already cut the file's actual class-(a)/(b)/(c) instances in this exact edit ('Cleaning is the compound move that keeps the loop fast.' [doctrine restatement], 'This is your stack.' / 'How far you take this is yours.' [self-referential/duplicate], 'The recognition is the point.' [aphorism kicker]) -- the maintainer note at raw line 97 cites this rule's own compounded source (2026-08-25-slides-three-low-value-bullet-classes.md) by date. No remaining low-value bullet found in the current body.
